What We Serve

The Menu

Every cup made to order. Beans sourced direct from farms we visit by name.

— 01

The Tideline Espresso

A double ristretto from our Pacific Blend — dark-roasted Yirgacheffe and Honduran washed. Syrupy body, hazelnut finish, dried cherry trailing through.

Espresso $4.50
— 02

Amber Wave Cortado

Equal parts ristretto and steamed whole milk — balanced, warm, poured into a ceramic glass thrown by a local Arcata potter. Unadulterated and true.

Espresso & Milk $5.25
— 03

Cold Fog Brew

Steeped 18 hours in cold Pacific spring water, never below 50°F. Smooth as sea glass. Served over a single hand-cut obsidian ice cube.

Cold Brew $6.00
— 04

Burnt Cedar Latte

Double espresso with house-smoked vanilla syrup and oat milk from a NorCal creamery — finished with a dusting of toasted cacao and a curl of orange zest.

Signature Latte $6.50
— 05

Saltmoor Chai

House masala blend — cardamom, black pepper, star anise — dark-steeped with coconut milk, finished with cold brew and a pinch of Humboldt sea salt.

Chai $5.75
— 06

Heather & Honey Flat White

Micro-foamed whole milk over a double ristretto, sweetened only with raw wildflower honey from Humboldt County. The coffee leads; the sweetness listens.

Flat White $5.75
Seasonal Rotation

Our bean selection turns with the harvest. Ask your barista what arrived this week — we keep two rotating single-origins on the bar at all times.

Our Story

Born from
Fog & Flame

"We started Driftwood because we couldn't find the coffee we wanted on the coast. So we learned to roast it ourselves."

Founded in 2018 in a converted boathouse on Humboldt Bay, Driftwood Roasters was built on a single conviction: proximity matters. We source direct from farms in Ethiopia, Honduras, and Colombia — growers we visit yearly, relationships built over shared meals and long conversations about soil and altitude.

Every bag that leaves our roastery carries the farm name, the varietal, and the exact date roasted. We roast in batches no larger than 22 pounds on a 1960s Probat drum roaster we restored ourselves over three winters. Coffee should be traceable all the way back to the tree.

Yirgacheffe, ET Huila, CO Santa Bárbara, HN Probat 1962
